title: TTFT surge triage, cross-deployment profiling and customer bridge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Urgent investigation and hotfix for a multi-customer TTFT (time-to-first-token) and tokens/sec regression observed across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. The regression appears under short-duration chat bursts and high fanout to larger models. Scope: reproduce across environments, produce a short-term mitigation for impacted customers, and roll a safe scheduler/prefetch hotfix with observability to validate recovery. Deliverables: repro harness, metrics dashboards, hotpatch PR, canary rollout plan, and customer communications.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:24 - Customer A reported 3-5x TTFT spikes for chat flows using model:redwood/open-7B in Hosted region us-west-2. Initial support capture attached. (support ticket #SUP-12943)

2026-03-12 11:10 - Reproduced locally on Dedicated with model variant open-7B-int8 when traffic pattern simulates 200 concurrent short chats. Observed large KV-prefetch fanout and microbatch handshake delays leading to queue amplification.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Added a temporary routing policy to steer affected customers to a lighter quantized variant (open-7B-int4-fallback) for Hosted while triage proceeds. Notified Customer A and Customer B of mitigation. Reduced TTFT by ~40% for those requests.

2026-03-13 08:50 - Heap and trace analysis: kernel selector misranked multi-tenant requests that had <32 tokens leading to oversized microbatch windows. This caused scheduling stalls and delayed first-token emission. Also saw amortized CPU lock contention in the prefetch worker loop on Private clusters with high simultaneous model fanout.

2026-03-13 12:00 - Design decision: implement two-phased fix: (1) emergency config cap on KV-prefetch concurrency + priority hedging for short-context requests, and (2) microkernel selector heuristic patch to prefer low-latency execution path for short sequences. Phase (1) is a runtime config change; Phase (2) requires kernel rollout and tests.

2026-03-13 16:20 - PR created for phase (1): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3842. PR implements a prefetch_concurrency cap and a short_context_fastpath toggle. Unit + integration tests added. Requesting urgent review from @marco and @li-chen.

2026-03-14 09:30 - Deployed phase (1) as a config override to Hosted control plane (canary group: 5% threads in us-west-2). Early telemetry: median TTFT improved from 380ms to 170ms across canary; tokens/sec recovered by ~25% for median short-chat workload.

2026-03-14 13:45 - Private customer cluster (on-prem) was given a recommended kubepatch and runtime flag. Customer C applied patch and confirmed TTFT reduction; follow-up to validate under their peak daily load scheduled for 2026-03-16.

2026-03-15 07:10 - Ongoing work on phase (2): kernel selector heuristic. Branch runtime/selector-fastpath-112 created. Performance microbench harness added under infra/tests/selector_harness. Need two perf signoffs: perf-team and reliability-team before wider rollout.

2026-03-15 10:05 - Customer D escalated via CSM: Dedicated pool experiencing intermittent tokens/sec collapse when model-fanout > 8. Assigned an owner for focused reproduction and parallel telemetry sampling. Added to incident bridge.

2026-03-15 12:40 - Next steps: finish kernel patch (ETA 2026-03-17), expand canary to 20% after smoke tests, prepare rollback instructions, and draft postmortem template. Schedule customer bridge for 2026-03-16 14:00 PST. Also add targeted eval prompt set to detect TTFT regressions in CI.

Links: Confluence runbook - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/TTFT+Surge+Triage; PR phase1 - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3842; selector branch - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/selector-fastpath-112; Support tickets - SUP-12943, SUP-12987.
acceptance_criteria: Consistent repro for TTFT spike in dedicated and hosted with synthetic short-chat workload
Phase (1) config hotpatch deployed to Hosted and validated (median TTFT improvement >= 30%)
Phase (2) kernel selector patch merged with performance regression <= 2% on long-context workloads
Canary expansion plan and rollback runbook reviewed and approved by reliability and infra on-call
Customer communications sent and impacted customers verified recovery
